title: Why You Automatically Step Back From People
hook: You have an invisible bubble around you.

narration.text: You have an invisible bubble around you.
When someone gets too close, you automatically step back.
This is your brain's social boundary alarm system.
It helps regulate comfort and safety in interactions.
This response is deep-seated, not just a personal preference.
Noticing it helps you understand social cues better.
If this surprised you, like the video and subscribe for more insights into your mind.

description: Ever wonder why you automatically step back when someone invades your personal space? It is a basic, unconscious social boundary response built into your brain. This video explains the fascinating mechanism behind this everyday reaction.
topic: Why you might automatically step back when someone invades your personal space. This is a basic social boundary response.
